verbatim_quote: Plastics, rubbers, proteins, epoxies, networks, gels, and such belong to the broad class of materials called polymers, because all of these materials have many small repeat units covalently bonded together. Polymers have unique physical properties due to their considerable molecular size, numerous conformations, and chemical variety. Their properties can be modulated by combining one or more polymers to make polymer blends or by adding nanoparticles to make polymer nanocomposites.

Within the Department of Materials Science and Engineering at Penn, we have expertise in a wide range of polymers including acid- and ion-containing polymers that can be used for tough thermoplastics and specialty membranes

Biomaterials encompass all classes of materials that are used in medical applications including tissue engineering, medical implants, and drug delivery. In MSE at Penn, polymers and inorganic materials are being developed to replace bone and blood vessels.
